title: Phase 5: Translation Batch Prefetching, Mobile App Parity & Offline Caching
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 5):

### Summary
Add intelligent viewport/list prefetching, offline translation fallback, and mobile app parity (`apps/mobile`).

### Scope
- **Batch Prefetching:**
  - Prefetch visible list items upon feed load (e.g. 20 prayers at once in a single `/api/translate` call).
  - Background warming of cache for frequently viewed contacts and pinned notes.
- **Mobile Parity (`apps/mobile`):**
  - Integrate translation service in React Native mobile views (Today, Prayers, Messages, People).
  - Use AsyncStorage for mobile L2 cache.
- **Offline & Fallback Polish:**
  - Graceful fallback to original text on network failure or rate limits with retry indicators.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Lists load with minimal perceived translation delay via batch prefetching.
- Mobile client supports full Spanish mode with cached translations.

title: Phase 4: Dynamic UGC Translation Integration across Prayers, People, Messages & Notes
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 4):

### Summary
Wire the translation hook and `<Translate />` component into dynamic User-Generated Content (UGC) across the application.

### Scope
- **Prayers & Testimonies:**
  - `PrayerList.tsx`, `AnsweredList.tsx`, and mobile `PrayerListMobile.tsx`.
  - Translate prayer burdens, prayer titles, update notes, and answered testimonies.
- **People & Directory:**
  - `ContactDetailsModal.tsx`, `Directory.tsx`, and `History.tsx`.
  - Translate contact notes, interaction log summaries, and next step reminders.
- **Messages & Chat:**
  - `Messages.tsx`, `chat.ts`, and mobile chat threads.
  - Live translation of incoming chat messages with reactive subscription.
- **Coordination Notes & The Board:**
  - `CoordinationNotes.tsx`, `EmbedCoordinationDoc.tsx`.
  - Markdown-aware translation preserving headings, checklists, links, and code blocks.
- **Original Content Switcher:**
  - Add an inline 'Ver original' / 'Show original' toggle for translated user cards.

### Acceptance Criteria
- User-entered text in any section translates seamlessly when Spanish is active.
- Clicking 'Ver original' toggles back to the raw source text.
- Comprehensive unit tests across components.

title: Phase 3: Static UI Strings Localization (i18n) for Shell, Modals & Navigation
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 3):

### Summary
Extract and localize all static UI strings (navigation tabs, buttons, modal headers, empty states, system alerts, and notifications) into an English/Spanish dictionary.

### Scope
- **UI Localization Dictionary (`src/locales/es.json` / `src/locales/en.json`):**
  - Navigation items: Coordination Notes, People, The Journey, On our hearts, History, Settings, More menu.
  - Action buttons: 'Add someone', 'Log a visit', 'Smart Import', 'Quick Add', 'Export CSV', 'Save', 'Cancel'.
  - Modal titles, empty state descriptions, error messages, and form labels.
- **Integration:**
  - Lightweight dictionary helper `t(key, fallback)` integrated with layout and language preference context.
  - Zero-latency, deterministic rendering for all chrome and static controls.

### Acceptance Criteria
- When Spanish is toggled on, all shell controls and UI buttons switch instantly to Spanish.
- Unit tests verify all dictionary keys exist and render correctly.

title: Phase 2: Client Translation Engine, Multi-Tier Caching & Language Preference Toggle
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 2):

### Summary
Implement the client-side translation engine, reactive hooks, multi-tier caching (L1 React state / memory + L2 IndexedDB / localStorage), and user language preference toggle.

### Scope
- **Translation Client Core (`src/lib/translator.ts`):**
  - Content hashing (SHA-256 / Murmur3) matching backend.
  - L1 (in-memory LRU) + L2 (IndexedDB / localStorage) client cache.
  - Request batcher & debouncer (50ms queue) calling `POST /api/translate`.
- **React Hooks & Primitives:**
  - `useTranslate(text, options)` hook.
  - `<Translate text={...} />` component with loading skeleton and error fallback.
- **Language Preference & UI Controls:**
  - Add `language?: 'en' | 'es'` to `userPreferences` schema and Firestore subscription.
  - Language toggle selector in `TopNav.tsx`, `MobileNav.tsx`, and `Settings.tsx`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Seamless synchronous lookup for already-cached translations with zero layout shift.
- Language toggle flips app preference and reactivity triggers live re-rendering.
- Full unit test coverage.

title: [Macro study] Expand the command palette + central shortcut registry
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Code**

## Problem

Keyboard handling is ad hoc and undiscoverable: `⌘K` in `GlobalSearch.tsx:295`, `⌘Enter` in `Thread.tsx`, `TodoComposer.tsx`, `LogVisitModal.tsx`, and `FeedbackFAB.tsx` — five separate listeners, no registry, nothing listed anywhere. The ⌘K palette offers four quick actions with no way to learn what else exists.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/` — a registry where every command declares its scope, description, condition, and handler, so the same registration both binds the key and populates the command palette. Shortcuts teach themselves.

## Explicitly NOT adopting

Their leader grammar (`c`+letter creates, `g`+letter goes) and vim navigation (`j`/`k`, `gg`, `shift+G`). Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day; this app serves students and Full-timers opening it a few times a week, often on a phone. Also skipping their priority chain and scope inheritance — far more machinery than this needs.

## Scope

- A small registry: id, scope, description, handler
- Both binds the shortcut and populates the ⌘K palette
- Migrate the five existing ad-hoc listeners onto it
- Palette lists available actions with their shortcuts

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every existing shortcut still works
- [ ] The palette lists actions the user can currently take, filtered by role
- [ ] Registering a command in one place makes it both bound and discoverable

title: [Macro study] Four new to-do creation entry points
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Code + light design**

## Problem

To-dos can be created from two places: highlighting a line on a Board page, and from an interaction. Macro's argument is that trackers go stale because logging costs a context switch — they made tasks creatable from seven places for exactly this reason.

## Scope — four new entry points

1. **From an attendance absence** — marking someone absent on the Gatherings screen is the exact moment someone thinks "I should check on them." Highest value of the four.
2. **From the visit log form** — `Visit.followUpTaskId` already exists in the data model, so this is wiring, not schema. Makes creating the follow-up part of writing the visit up rather than a separate step.
3. **From a chat message** — hover / long-press → "Make a to-do", carrying the message as source. Mirrors the Board highlight flow already built.
4. **From a prayer** — turn a burden into a concrete follow-up while keeping the prayer linked as source.

## Implementation note

One shared helper over `addTodo` in `src/lib/todos.ts`; each site differs only in which source it links. The existing `sourceDocId` / `sourceInteractionId` pattern extends naturally.

## Design needed

Small — the affordance in four placements. Reuse the existing "Make a to-do" treatment from the Board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four create a to-do linked back to its source
- [ ] The source is visible on the resulting to-do row
- [ ] Available on mobile where the source screen exists

title: [Macro study] One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · ⚠️ **Has a privacy consequence — read before designing**

## Problem

A conversation about one person can live in three places today:

1. `contacts/{id}/threads` — the walking-together thread (Trainee-visible)
2. The Comments tab in `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (~line 2079) — gated `role === "admin" || isAdmin`, **Full-timers only**
3. Messages, with the contact attached via `ChatAttachment`

Someone asking "what did we say about Sarah?" has to check all three.

## What Macro does

*"Every deal gets its own channel, automatically, pinned right to the deal record."* Their argument: a CRM comment box always loses to where the conversation really happens, because people comment *and then* go ping the channel anyway. So the record's notes ARE the chat system, not a parallel one.

## ⚠️ Blocker — decide before this is designed

The Comments tab is Full-timer-only; the walking-together thread is Trainee-visible. **Merging them changes who can read pastoral oversight notes that were written under a different expectation.** This is a privacy change, not just a data migration. Pick one:

- **(recommended)** Migrated comments carry a visibility flag and the merged thread filters by role — preserves the original audience while still giving one place to look. Costs a `firestore.rules` change.
- Comments migrate into a Full-timer-only section of the merged thread.
- Existing comments stay in place; only *new* conversation goes to the thread.

## Scope

- `contacts/{id}/threads` becomes the single conversation surface
- Comments migrated per the decision above, with a migration script
- Attaching a contact in Messages links into that same thread rather than starting a parallel one
- `firestore.rules` updated and reproduced against the emulator **before** the rule is edited (rules deploys have their own CI gate — budget for it)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visibility decision recorded in this issue before design starts
- [ ] No existing comment becomes readable by someone who could not read it before
- [ ] Emulator-backed rules tests, red before green
- [ ] Migration is reversible or dry-runnable

title: [Macro study] Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Blocked on #326 (read/done model) and #327 (date bucketing)

## Problem

"What needs my attention" is split across three surfaces:

- My Day's hand-assembled sections (`src/views/MyDay.tsx`, 1,192 lines)
- `FromTraineesInbox` — the Full-timer oversight feed
- `NotificationCenter` — the bell, a separate list entirely

Someone has to check all three to know where they stand. And `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` only tracks *scanned*, which is passive — without a "done", the list only grows, so it stops being a list anyone can finish, and people stop opening it.

## What Macro does

One list holding email, messages, @mentions, task assignments, and agent results. `e` marks done and removes the item. Their framing: *"You can think of the Signal view as your action list."* The stance is that you should check exactly one thing.

**Not adopting:** their AI-sorted Signal/Noise split (volume doesn't justify it, and the failure mode — AI hides something pastoral — is worse than the problem), and Inbox-Zero-as-pressure. A list of people you haven't followed up with is not disposable the way email is; "clearing" a person is a strange verb, and a UI that rewards emptying the list can teach people to dismiss rather than follow up. Take *"done is distinct from seen"*; leave the pressure to reach zero.

## Scope

- One attention feed on My Day carrying team activity, to-do assignments, thread questions, and notifications
- Explicit per-row "done" that removes it, built on #326
- Date-group headers from #327
- Bell becomes push delivery only, not a second list

## Design needed

Row anatomy per item kind, the done affordance, group headers, empty state. Desktop, `MyDayMobile.tsx`, and `apps/mobile/`.

## Watch

The feed reads contacts, interactions, a `collectionGroup` over threads, notifications, and to-dos. My Day already does several of these — measure read volume before adding more, and check whether new composite indexes are needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One feed replaces the three surfaces; the bell no longer maintains a parallel list
- [ ] Marking done removes the row and persists per-user
- [ ] Each of the four roles sees an appropriate feed
- [ ] Firestore read count per load measured and recorded

title: [Macro study] Audit and derive Contact activity fields
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only**

## Problem

`Contact` carries `lastSeen`, `lastContactedDate`, `lastContactedBy`, `lastContactedById`, and `hasNewActivity`. All of these look derivable from interactions, visits, and attendance — but if any is hand-entered, or written at only some of the call sites, it goes stale silently. A stale `lastContactedDate` breaks exactly the question the app exists to answer: who have we not seen in a while.

## What Macro does

From their CRM docs: *"records create themselves … stages are all manual: Macro doesn't yet know where a company lies in your pipeline and relies on you."* A clean line between what the system can observe and what only a person knows. Their "Last Interaction" is a sortable column precisely because it is never typed.

Stage stays manual here too — that is judgment, and correctly a human's.

## Scope

1. Map every write of the five fields across web (`src/lib/`, `src/views/`, `src/components/modals/`) and `apps/mobile/`
2. Route them through one derived update triggered by logging an interaction, a visit, or an attendance mark
3. Remove any path that accepts them as direct user input

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Logging an interaction, a visit, and an attendance mark each update the fields identically
- [ ] No UI writes these fields directly
- [ ] Tests cover all three event types
- [ ] Audit findings recorded in the issue before the fix lands, so the size of the drift is known

title: [Macro study] Frecency ranking in Global Search
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Highest value-per-line item in the study

## Problem

`src/components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx` does substring filtering, caps each group at `GS_MAX = 4`, and applies **no ranking**. With no query, "recent people" sorts by `updatedAt` — which is *someone else's* edit, not your usage. So the people you open every day are not the people you are shown.

## What Macro does

`crates/frecency` computes, per user per entity:

```
frequency = log2(event_count + 2)
recency   = Σ over last 10 events of  exp(-0.1 × hours_ago) × weight
score     = 0.7 × frequency + 0.3 × recency

weights:  open = +2.0,  ping = 0.0,  close = -1.0
```

The negative close weight is the interesting part: opening something and immediately closing it is evidence it was the *wrong* result, so it demotes itself.

Their own client ships a much cheaper version for the command palette — `apps/web/src/features/command/recency.ts` is ~20 lines, a persisted `Record<commandId, timestamp>`. **That is the version to copy**, not the Rust service.

## Scope

- Track opens in a per-uid localStorage store, reusing the pub/sub pattern already in `src/lib/inboxReads.ts`
- Rank results by score; keep the substring filter as the gate (frecency only orders what already matched)
- Consider whether `GS_MAX = 4` should rise once ordering is meaningful

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a contact repeatedly floats it to the top of the no-query list
- [ ] Open-then-immediately-close does not promote a result
- [ ] Scoring is a pure function with unit tests; storage is tested separately

title: [Macro study] Shared date bucketing util (Today / Yesterday / This Week / Older)
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Feeds the merged attention feed's grouping

## Problem

Date grouping is implemented inline in History, My Day, and the activity feed, each slightly differently. The merged attention feed will want the same grouping, which would make a fourth copy.

## What Macro does

`crates/models_grouping/src/date_buckets.rs` — a fixed vocabulary as three tiny pure functions:

| Bucket | Range | Order |
|---|---|---|
| Today | 0 days | 0 |
| Yesterday | 1 day | 1 |
| This Week | 2–6 days | 2 |
| Last Week | 7–13 days | 3 |
| This Month | 14–30 days | 4 |
| Last Month | 31–60 days | 5 |
| Older | 61+ days | 6 |

Their docs frame it as a product feature, not formatting: it "keeps a busy list scannable without changing any of your filters or sorting."

## Scope

`bucketFor(date)`, `bucketLabel(key)`, `bucketOrder(key)` in a shared util, built on the existing `daysSince` / `parseMs` in `src/components/landing/helpers.ts`. Adopt in History, My Day, and the activity feed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three pure functions, no view imports
- [ ] Unit tests at every boundary: 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 30, 31, 60, 61 days
- [ ] Existing groupings in History / My Day / activity render identically or better
- [ ] Warm labels agreed — the app says "Looking back", not "This Month", so copy should match the app's voice rather than Macro's

title: [Macro study] Unify read/done state into one per-user model
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · **Prerequisite for the merged attention feed**

## Problem

Five mechanisms currently answer fragments of one question — "has this person seen / dealt with this?":

- `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` — localStorage, per-uid, ids like `contact:<id>` (already an entity ref)
- `src/lib/convHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden conversations
- `src/lib/messageHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden messages
- `Notification.readBy` / `dismissedBy` — Firestore arrays
- `Contact.reviewed` — a boolean on the shared domain object

Three storage strategies, no shared vocabulary. `Contact.reviewed` is the worst of them: it puts a per-user workflow state onto a shared record, so when two Full-timers walk with the same trainee it is ambiguous who reviewed it.

## What Macro does

Separates two orthogonal axes and applies both uniformly to any entity: **read** (I have seen it) and **done** (I have dealt with it). `inboxReads` today only models "scanned", which is passive — there is no way to clear something off your list.

## Scope

- One per-user store keyed by entity ref (`contact:<id>`, `interaction:<id>`, `thread:<id>` — the shape `inboxReads.ts` already uses), with `read` and `done` as separate axes.
- Migrate `inboxReads`, `convHides`, `messageHides` behind it.
- Leave `Notification.readBy` alone for now — it is genuinely shared state, not a per-device preference.
- Plan the `Contact.reviewed` migration but do not remove the field in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing inbox-read and hide behaviour is unchanged from the user's point of view
- [ ] A `done` axis exists and is independently settable from `read`
- [ ] Unit tests cover set/clear/subscribe on both axes and the migration from each legacy store

title: [Macro study] Adopt product patterns from the Macro codebase (tracking)
label: CLOSED
body:
Tracking issue for work adopting product patterns from a read-only study of [macro-inc/macro](https://github.com/macro-inc/macro) (AGPLv3, SolidJS + Rust all-in-one workspace).

## Why

Macro's CRM, tasks, docs, and channels map closely onto People/The Journey, to-dos, Coordination Notes, and Messages. Their product decisions are stances rather than infrastructure, so they port even though none of their code does. Their core arguments:

- **Trackers go stale** because logging costs a context switch — so make creating an entry possible from wherever the decision is actually made.
- **Records should build themselves**; only judgment (stage) is manual.
- **You should check one thing** to know what needs your attention, and "done" must be a real verb distinct from "seen."
- **A record's notes ARE the chat system** — a separate comments box always loses to where the conversation really happens.

## Scaled down deliberately

Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day. This app serves four roles who open it a few times a week, often on a phone. Keyboard-first navigation (vim keys, `c`/`g` leader grammar) was evaluated and **declined**; splits/window management, the filter AST, the properties system, and AI Signal/Noise sorting were also declined as poor fits.

## Scope multiplier

Every design-touching item lands in up to three places: the desktop view, its `*Mobile.tsx` twin (7 such pairs exist), and the React Native app in `apps/mobile/`. This is the main reason the code-only foundation goes first — it is written once and shared.

## Phase 1 — foundation, code only, unblocked

Nothing here needs design input; all four can proceed in parallel.

- [ ] #326 — Unify read/done state into one per-user model **(prerequisite for the merged feed)**
- [ ] #327 — Shared date bucketing util **(feeds the merged feed's grouping)**
- [ ] #328 — Frecency ranking in Global Search
- [ ] #329 — Audit and derive Contact activity fields

## Phase 2 — design assets

Merged attention feed · shared row action menu · contact pill + hover preview · merged thread tab · role-aware first-run checklist · four "Make a to-do" affordances.

## Phase 3 — build against the designs

- [ ] #330 — Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
- [ ] #331 — Notification stacking by target
- [ ] #332 — Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
- [ ] #333 — One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab ⚠️ **has a privacy decision to make first**
- [ ] #334 — Live contact pill with hover preview
- [ ] #335 — Role-aware first-run checklist
- [ ] #336 — Four to-do creation entry points
- [ ] #337 — Expand the ⌘K palette + central shortcut registry

## Testing

Per `CLAUDE.md` §6 all of this is logic/data/permissions code, so TDD is mandatory — failing test first. Coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts` ratchet up only.

title: Auto-create a GitHub issue when feedback is submitted
label: CLOSED
body:
## Context / Problem
Feedback submitted through the in-app feedback module (the "Leave a note" FAB and the `/feedback` page) lands only in the Firestore `feedback` collection and the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`). There is no bridge into our engineering workflow, so actionable feedback has to be manually re-entered as GitHub issues. We want submissions to automatically open a GitHub issue in this repo so they show up in normal triage.

## Proposed behavior
When a user submits feedback, automatically open a GitHub issue in `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`:
- **Trigger on all four kinds** — thought, idea, "something's off", request.
- Map kind → labels: `off` → `bug`; `thought`/`idea`/`request` → `enhancement`; plus a new `feedback` label (needs creating).
- Title: short summary from the kind + first line of the message.
- Body: full message, submitter name/email, kind, and a link to the admin feedback entry.
- **Link back:** store the created issue's number/URL on the feedback doc and show a "View on GitHub" link in the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`).
- **Best-effort:** a GitHub failure must NOT block or revert the in-app success state (mirror the existing `logActivity` / `sendNotification` pattern).

## Suggested implementation
- Feedback is written client-side directly to Firestore today (`addDoc(collection(db, 'feedback'), …)`) in `src/components/FeedbackFAB.tsx` and `src/views/SubmitFeedback.tsx`. Keep that write; add a best-effort backend call afterward.
- Add an endpoint (e.g. `POST /api/feedback/github-issue`) in `server.ts` (Express on Cloud Run, fronted by the Cloudflare proxy in `functions/api/[[path]].ts`) that creates the issue via the GitHub REST API and writes the issue URL/number back onto the feedback doc with the Admin SDK.
- Store a `GITHUB_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT with Issues:write on this repo, or a GitHub App token) as a Cloud Run env var — never exposed to the client.
- Create a `feedback` label in the repo.
- Add optional `githubIssueUrl` / `githubIssueNumber` to the `Feedback` type (`src/types.ts`) and render the link in `src/views/FeedbackList.tsx`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Submitting any feedback kind opens a GitHub issue with appropriate labels.
- The issue references the submitter + message; the feedback doc / admin list links to the issue.
- A GitHub outage does not break feedback submission.

---
_Filed as a tracking issue; implementation not started yet._

title: Move Firestore-rules deploy to keyless auth (Workload Identity Federation)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Goal
Replace the long-lived service-account **key** used by the Firestore-rules deploy with **keyless auth via Workload Identity Federation (WIF)** — GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged for short-lived GCP credentials, so there's no JSON key stored in a GitHub secret.

> Terminology: for CI/workloads this is **Workload Identity Federation** (a *Workload* Identity Pool + OIDC provider). "Workforce pools" are the sibling feature for human users from an external IdP — not what we want here.

## Why
Follow-up to #44 / #46. Today [`.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml`](.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml) (lines 76–79) authenticates with:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
  with:
    credentials_json: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
```

That secret holds a **long-lived private key** for `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Downsides:
- A non-expiring credential sits in GitHub secrets; if it leaks, it's valid until manually revoked.
- No rotation story — keys silently age forever (`validBeforeTime: 9999`).
- During #46 we hit exactly the failure mode this invites: the secret was holding the *wrong* SA's key and nobody could tell (secrets are write-only). WIF removes the key entirely.

With WIF: tokens are minted per-run, expire in minutes, and access is scoped by an attribute condition to **this repo only**.

## Current state (already in place)
- Deploy SA `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` exists and holds the 3 roles a rules deploy needs: `roles/firebaserules.admin`, `roles/datastore.indexAdmin`, `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer`.
- Project: `sac-campus-hub` (project number `914549253362`).
- Repo: `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`.

## Setup (one-time, GCP side)
```bash
PROJECT_ID=sac-campus-hub
PROJECT_NUMBER=914549253362
POOL=github-actions
PROVIDER=github
REPO=Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker
SA=github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 1. Workload Identity Pool
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create "$POOL" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --display-name="GitHub Actions"

# 2. OIDC provider, locked to this repo (the attribute-condition is required)
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc "$PROVIDER" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --workload-identity-pool="$POOL" \
  --display-name="GitHub" \
  --issuer-uri="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository=assertion.repository" \
  --attribute-condition="assertion.repository == '${REPO}'"

# 3. Let this repo's tokens impersonate the deploy SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --role="roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser" \
  --member="principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL}/attribute.repository/${REPO}"
```
Provider resource name for the workflow:
`projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github`

## Workflow change
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write        # required for OIDC

# ...in the deploy job, replace the auth step:
  - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
    uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    with:
      project_id: sac-campus-hub
      workload_identity_provider: projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github
      service_account: github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
The action still exports `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (now a short-lived token file), so the `firebase deploy` step needs no change. Update the file's header comment (lines 6–9) which currently describes the key-based flow.

## Cutover & cleanup (after a green WIF run)
- [ ] Confirm `workflow_dispatch` + a real push both deploy green via WIF.
- [ ] Delete the GitHub secret `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`.
- [ ] Delete `github-action@`'s user-managed key `63fafb9d4edaa333c8060133ed5814a41419b9e9`
      (`gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete …`) so no long-lived key remains.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WIF pool + OIDC provider created, scoped to `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`.
- [ ] `github-action@` granted `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` for the repo's principalSet.
- [ ] Workflow uses `workload_identity_provider` + `service_account`, with `id-token: write`.
- [ ] Deploy is green with **no** `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret present.
- [ ] Old key and secret removed.

_Refs: #44 (auto-deploy), #46 (credential validation + the wrong-key incident)._

title: Inconsistent error state across data views (stuck skeletons / silent failures on Firestore errors)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Background

`handleFirestoreError` (`src/lib/firebase.ts:68`) **throws** after logging. PR #43 fixed the cases where a `setLoading(false)` sat *after* the throw (dead code → skeleton stuck forever). But that PR deliberately left a broader gap: **there is no consistent error state across the data views.**

Today data views (Attendance, Dashboard, MyDay, Directory, OutreachBoard, History, PrayerList) only track `loading`. On a list error there are two bad outcomes:

1. **Stuck skeleton** — if the listener that owns `setLoading(false)` is the one that errors, loading never clears.
2. **Silent empty/partial list** — if a *different* listener errors after loading was already cleared, the user just sees missing/empty data with no indication anything failed.

Users can't distinguish "no data yet" / "empty" / "load failed", and there's no reusable error UI (only `Settings`/`SignUp` have local form-level `error` state).

## Affected listeners (error callbacks that never clear/​surface state)

Multi-listener views where `setLoading(false)` is only in the *first* success callback, so other listeners' errors are invisible and the owning listener's error hangs the skeleton:
- `src/views/Dashboard.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:83` (contacts success); error callbacks at `:85` `:91` `:97` `:103` `:133` `:142`
- `src/views/MyDay.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:113`; error callbacks at `:115` `:121` `:127` `:133` `:161` `:170` `:189`
- `src/views/History.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:252` (activities success); error callbacks at `:230` (contacts) `:254` (activities)

Secondary listeners with no error surface (loading driven by a sibling listener):
- `src/views/Directory.tsx` — contacts `:152`, interactions `:202`, comments `:211`
- `src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx` — contacts `:305`, interactions `:342`, comments `:351`
- `src/views/Attendance.tsx` — contacts `:98`

## Options considered (pick one when scheduled)

1. **Shared error UI + retry (recommended)** — add an `error` state per data view, set it in each error callback (before the throw), and render one reusable component, e.g. `Couldn't load {label} — Reload`. Distinguishes failure from empty; recoverable. (`onSnapshot` auto-retries on reconnect, but permission-denied won't recover — a `location.reload()` action is the practical retry.)
2. **Shared error message, no retry** — same component, display-only.
3. **Just clear loading everywhere** — generalize PR #43 so every error callback clears loading before the throw. No more stuck skeletons, but failures still look like empty lists (no explicit error message).

## Notes
- Keep the established ordering invariant: **clear state before calling `handleFirestoreError`**, since it throws (see PR #43 and `CoordinationNotes.tsx` as the reference).
- Whatever the choice, apply it uniformly to all the views/listeners listed above for consistency.

title: The Journey board: header count mismatch + 'Add to {stage}' doesn't prefill stage
label: CLOSED
body:
Two cosmetic/UX follow-ups found while reviewing the Outreach Board reskin ([PR #28](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/pull/28), Overhaul #12). Neither is a crash or data issue — splitting them out so #28 can land.

## 1. Header total doesn't reconcile with the per-stage breakdown

In [`src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx`](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/blob/main/src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx) the prose header bolds `filteredContacts.length` (which **includes** unmapped/unassigned contacts) but the per-stage breakdown sums only `getStageContactsArr(s.label).length` for **active** stages.

**Effect:** when any contact has a stage not in the active stages list (shown in the separate "Unassigned" column), the numbers don't add up — e.g. *"10 people walking it — 2 first contact, 3 second contact, 3 regular"* (sums to 8, not 10). Looks like a bug to the user.

**Fix options:** base the bold count on the per-stage sum, or append an "N unassigned" term when `unmappedContacts.length > 0`.

## 2. "Add to {stage}" / "Welcome someone new" footer buttons don't prefill the stage

The column footer buttons call `openNewContact()`, which opens the new-contact modal with **no stage argument** (`useLayout().openNewContact: () => setIsNewContactModalOpen(true)` in `src/App.tsx`).

**Effect:** clicking *"Add to Regular"* and saving lands the contact in the modal's default stage, not Regular — the label overpromises. The "Unassigned" column's *"Add to Unassigned"* is likewise misleading.

**Fix options:** thread an optional `initialStage` through `openNewContact` / `NewContactModal` and prefill it, or soften the labels (e.g. a single "Welcome someone new" everywhere) until prefill is wired.

---
_Found during local code review of #28; the PR-Reviewer bot rated #12 fully compliant. Out of scope for #28 (reskin-only)._

title: Account switching: session sometimes fails to persist after quick re-login
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
While verifying the role-based permissions in a real browser (signing in as each of the four role test users), I hit two problems related to **switching between user accounts**.

## 1. Log out control can be unreachable (primary, actionable)
The **Log out** button lives in the sidebar footer (`src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`, the `mt-auto` footer block). The sidebar (`h-screen`, `overflow-hidden`) and its nav-items container are both `overflow-hidden`, so on **shorter viewports** the footer can be pushed below the fold for roles that show many nav items:

- **Full-timer (admin)** and **Trainee (manager)** see all **7** nav items → the footer (Log out / Collapse) is clipped and not clickable.
- **Student (operator, 5)** and **Community (viewer, 3)** have fewer items → logout is reachable.

**Impact:** an admin/manager on a laptop with a shorter window (or OS chrome reducing height) may be unable to log out / switch accounts from the desktop sidebar.

**Repro:** sign in as an admin, shrink the window height (~660px content), observe the Log out button is not visible/clickable in the sidebar.

**Suggested fix:** make the nav-items region scrollable (`overflow-y-auto`) instead of `overflow-hidden`, and/or guarantee the footer is always pinned/visible regardless of item count.

## 2. Session occasionally fails to persist right after re-login (secondary, lower confidence)
When logging out and signing back in as a different user **quickly**, the new sign-in sometimes does not stick — the app returns to the welcome/sign-in screen instead of the dashboard, and a retry is needed. This was intermittent and may be a Firebase auth-persistence timing issue when a sign-in happens immediately after a sign-out/reload. Worth confirming whether real users hit it (e.g. shared kiosk / quick account switches).

## Context
Found during PR #3 (role-based access control). The permission logic itself works correctly for all four roles; this issue is specifically about the **logout / account-switching UX**.
